reading: The 6x6 top panel (above the 5-separator) is a 3x3 pattern drawn in 2x2 blocks; shrink it to 3x3. The 6x6 bottom panel is a mask: the 18x18 output has a copy of the 3x3 pattern in each 3x3 block whose mask cell is non-zero, empty elsewhere.

slots.mask: bottom panel below the separator (6x6), non-zero cells
slots.layout: output block (i,j) = unit if mask(i,j) else empty; output size = mask size x unit size

why: output = kron(mask != 0, downscaled top panel) on every pair

reading: Every isolated grey cell is replaced by a 3x3 stamp centred on it: grey corners, blue edges, empty centre.
why: each marker becomes the centre of an identical 3x3 pattern 5 1 5 / 1 0 1 / 5 1 5

reading: Each shape has one odd key cell; the shape swaps its main and key colours. The grid corners hold colour cells; at each such corner, the union of the (5x5-box) shapes whose key colour equals that corner colour is drawn in that colour, flush in the corner.
verb: swap colours and collect shapes into corners

slots.objects: multi-colour shapes, each with one key cell of a second colour
slots.swap: main colour <-> key colour inside each shape
slots.corner glyph: for each non-background grid corner of colour k: overlay of all shapes with key colour k, normalised to their box, placed in that corner, painted k

why: corner colour = key colour of the shapes gathered there; shapes keep position with swapped colours

reading: A lattice of framed tiles; most tile centres share one colour but a few have rare colours. Between two rare-coloured centres of the same colour on one row or column, the empty gap cells (0) are filled with that colour; frames and other tiles are not painted.

new_rows.name: rare_between
new_rows.datalog:
pcount(C, count(Y, X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rank(C, count(D)) :- pcount(C, N), pcount(D, M), M > N.
rare(C) :- rank(C, R), R >= 3.
rare_between(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), px(Y, X1, C), rare(C), px(Y, X2, C), X1 < X, X < X2.
rare_between(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), px(Y1, X, C), rare(C), px(Y2, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.

why: every 0-cell lying on a row or column between two cells of the same rare colour (fewer cells than gap, frame and common-centre colours) takes that rare colour

reading: The grid is symmetric (both mirror axes and diagonals) except for patches of 4 that hide cells; each 4 is replaced by its mirror-image cell.
why: output is symmetric about the grid's central axes; only 4-cells change

reading: A cup-shaped object sits on the bottom row with a different inner colour in its base. From just outside the two ends of the cup's top row, diagonal rays go up and outward to the border, painted in the inner colour.

slots.origin: the cells diagonally up-left of the top row's left end and up-right of its right end

why: two diagonal lines of the inner colour, one per side, from the cup's top corners to the border

reading: Panels separated by frame lines each show the same small object, shifted vertically by a constant step from panel to panel; the output is one panel with the object moved one more step.

slots.panels: stripes cut by the full separator columns
slots.subject: the small object in each panel
slots.output: a single panel with the object at last position + step

why: object positions form an arithmetic sequence across panels; output continues it (pair 1 lands one row further than a strict step would give)

reading: In every third column (columns 0, 3, 6, ...), yellow cells become magenta.

new_rows.name: every_third
new_rows.datalog:
third(X) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0.
third(X2) :- third(X), X2 = X + 3, px(Y, X2, C).
every_third(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), third(X).

why: cells with column index divisible by 3 map 4 -> 6 (0 stays 0); all other cells unchanged

reading: Left 4x4 panel is a blue shape with holes; right 4x4 panel holds a coloured shape. If the coloured shape occupies exactly the holes (same positions), it is dropped into them; otherwise the output is the left panel unchanged.

slots.condition: piece cells == base's 0 cells, position for position
slots.result: base overlaid with piece if condition holds, else base

why: filled in pairs 0,2,4,6 where the piece is the exact complement; unchanged in 1,3,5 where it is not
invariants: output is the left panel's size

reading: Two red cells mark the ends of a straight line (row, column or diagonal). Cells strictly between them are recoloured: 0 becomes red, blue becomes green.

new_rows.name: line2
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 2).
line2(Y, X) :- two(Y, X1), two(Y, X2), X1 < X, X < X2, px(Y, X, C).
line2(Y, X) :- two(Y1, X), two(Y2, X), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, px(Y, X, C).
line2(Y, X) :- two(Y1, X1), two(Y2, X2), Y1 < Y2, D = Y2 - Y1, X2 = X1 + D, px(Y, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, K = Y - Y1, X = X1 + K.
line2(Y, X) :- two(Y1, X1), two(Y2, X2), Y1 < Y2, D = Y2 - Y1, X1 = X2 + D, px(Y, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, K = Y - Y1, X = X1 - K.

why: on the segment between the two 2-cells, 0 -> 2 and 1 -> 3; nothing off the segment changes
